prompts: Can you walk me through what actually happens when I click a block with the Fill tool (N)? Start from window_fill.py. I want to know which cells it picks, what each mode does (Draw, Shift/Erase, Clone), why the build grid disappears while it is selected, what stops it hanging on a huge area, and what World.fill_region keeps in sync when it writes. I don't care about the undo stack for this one.

Twice now a save has gone wrong (once the disk was nearly full, once it threw an exception mid-save) and afterwards the .wld on disk was empty or cut off, so I lost the map I already had. A failed save should leave the old file alone. Please make the normal Save path (worldio.write_to, then write_packed) safe, and add a test. Leave write_payload as it is.

How does Copy/Paste decide which block to put down when I copy on a map and paste inside a voxel prefab's model canvas, or the other way round? What happens to a block type the other side doesn't have, and to the canvas's custom colours when I paste them into a map? Also, does the 'Pasted N blocks' count ever lie on the canvas?

I cut an inset ladder up the side of a cliff, then ran the Smooth brush along the cliff top to round it off. The ladder's top rung turned into a ramp. On a thin wall the top rung's ladder tag just vanished, and Shift-smoothing removes it as well. Smoothing should only reshape terrain and leave ladders alone. Please fix it in the Smooth brush (window_shape.py) and in the agent-side smooth_area (gamekit_shapes.py), which probably has the same problem, with tests.

When I copy a section of roof made with the Shape tool (slopes, corners, slabs) and paste it elsewhere on the map, I get plain cubes. Copy should remember each block's shape tag and paste should put it back, map to map, in editor.py's copy and paste; chop marks are out of scope. The model canvas can't use shape tags, so a paste there should stay plain blocks. One Ctrl+Z should undo the paste and its tags together. Please add tests.

editor.py repeats the same geometry several times. The rectangle outline and fill loops appear twice in cells_for_shape (RECT, and the two-cell-wide CIRCLE fallback), and the ellipse centre and radius setup is written out in cells_for_shape, cells_for_volume and volume_occupancy. Pull those into small helpers without changing any output. volume_occupancy and volume_shell_bounds must stay exactly equal to cells_for_volume, and the editor tests must still pass.
